title: Apply for a property certificate under mutual recognition
summary: You can apply for an equivalent property certificate in NSW if you hold a property certificate from another Australian state, territory, or New Zealand.
intro:
If you hold an interstate property certificate, you may be eligible to apply for the equivalent in NSW.

A property certificate of registration lets you work as an assistant agent in:

Applications can be lodged online or at a Service NSW Centre.
who_can_apply: Hold a current and equivalent certificate of registration in another Australian state/territory or New Zealand.
Have your principal place of business in NSW or within 50 kilometres of the NSW border.
what_you_need: Two proof of identity documents (such as Australian driver licence, Medicare card, passport).
The required forms (e.g., Notice for Registration of Equivalent Occupation – PDF, Application for Certificate of Registration – PDF).

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to complete your application.
Gather original copies of the required supporting documents, as indicated on the form.
Visit a service centre to submit your application and payment.

faqs.q: What is a property certificate of registration?
faqs.a: A property certificate of registration allows you to work as an assistant agent.

faqs.q: Where can I apply for the property certificate?
faqs.a: Applications can be lodged online or at a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to apply?
faqs.a: You need two proof of identity documents (such as Australian driver licence, Medicare card, passport), the required forms, and payment.
